chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Going commercial; John Hammond; the Casa Loma sound
summary: McRae tells Hammond to stay quiet about the band's change toward pop, and recalls Glen Gray finding his sound.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And John Hammond say -- he was writing for a paper -- I forget what paper he writes for. John used to come up and say, "Oh, yall changing the band."

I say, "John, if you're going to write anything about the band, (if you can't write anything good) (inadible), don't write anything at all, because right now we don't need no bad publicity," you know.
Who's that? Melody Maker he would write it for.
Yeah.
In England.
Yeah. I say if you're going to write anything about the band, if you ain't going to write something good, just don't write anything, you know. You're our friend, don't write --

I say, "Look, (inaudible) we're, right at now, we're going commercial. Chick feels that we have did all we could do with where we were. We want to make a move. We wanna"--
And you know, at that time Benny was trying to get a band together, then Casa Loma --
Benny Carter?
And Glen Gray, you know. Up there in the Bronx (there, inaudible) he was trying to get his thing together.
One thing, he called Chick Webb up and told him -- he say, "Look, I'm looking for a sound."
He hadn't heard this sound. He said, "I'm looking for a sound." And (one day we got a call, say inaudible). "What yall doing today, tomorrow's Saturday? Come up I want you to hear something."
And we went up -- Chick and I, (and Ella inaudible), heard this beautiful sound. (That's it, inaudible), That's it. That sound is beautiful. I've been looking for that sound!"
Now this is his own

Glen Gray's band.
He hadn't taken over the Casa Loma at the time? Or, was this a Casa Loma band?
I think it was the Casa Loma.
Okay.
The band he made famous. He was looking for a sound.
Okay, that was the Casa Loma Band that he took over.

Yeah. He say, 'I'm looking for a sound, you know. I haven't got it yet.' And he got it. He finally got it. Like it was in the picture. He was looking for something, and he found it. And he called us up and say, 'Come on, listen to this.' We say, 'Man, that's beautiful.' But in the meantime, we were working with Jack, (Unaudible) -- Robbins' music -- Shapiro
